From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ari@peregrinehealth.com, morgan@peregrinehealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Immediate help: sustained 504s, throughput drop (Peregrine prod)

Stack summary so far (observed by SRE):
- Around 08:48 PT a config change (deploy INF-8409) incrementally increased kv-cache TTL granularity and changed the cache key normalization for certain hot prefixes; that landed to the us-west-2 hotpath.
- Result: large increase in cache misses for several high-volume prefixes => sudden spike in KV cache fill activity. That, combined with increased bundling of requests (we saw batching windows expand past 35ms), created KV thrash + longer per-request CPU on the runtime path.
- The runtime's queue (per-host request queue) grew to >2.2k pending requests, which triggered timeouts (504) and amplified client retry storms.

Immediate mitigations applied at 09:30 PT (by David):
- Disabled continuous batching for Peregrine route (hotpatch), and reduced max_batch_ms from 40 -> 8 for that route only.
- Reverted the new cache key normalization for the affected prefixes (partial rollback flag).
- Raised per-host concurrency cap for the pool from 64 -> 80 to allow steady throughput while cache warms.

Preliminary numbers: error rate dropped from ~18% -> ~4% within 6 minutes; tail latency p95 from ~950ms -> ~270ms. We're continuing to monitor.

Action items:
- Karthik / runtime team: confirm why batching window widened simultaneously; check telemetry around batch timer resets and kernel scheduling.
- David: collect host-level traces, kernel latencies, and kv-cache metrics; attach to INF-8412.
- Hannah: coordinate exec brief with Peregrine CTO if they request it — propose 1600 PT.

Marissa
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Immediate help: sustained 504s, throughput drop (Peregrine prod)

Adding technical context: the batching timer is cooperative and is sensitive to wake latency on the VM; we see a small spike in kernel scheduler latency correlated with a systemd CPU isolator bump from an unrelated job. That likely increased effective max_batch_ms observed by the runtime. Combined with increased cache coldness, requests stayed in batch longer and expanded batch sizes.

For next steps I recommend:
- Short-term: keep the hotpatch in place for 2 hours and perform a controlled canary rollback of INF-8409 across a subset of hosts (we already reverted keys for affected prefixes).
- Medium-term: add a safety throttle so that if queue depth > 1000 we clamp batching aggressively and emit an early_kv_miss metric to prioritize cache-side healing.

I'll own the canary rollback plan (INF-8413) and coordinate with David on telemetry.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Ari / Morgan —

Quick update from the field: we applied targeted mitigations at 09:30 PT (details below) and have seen a substantial improvement. Key points: 
- What we did: disabled continuous batching on your route, reduced max_batch_ms to 8ms, reverted the cache-key normalization for affected prefixes, and temporarily increased per-host concurrency.
- Impact: 504/error rate dropped from ~18% to ~2% for the /generate route; p95 latency moved from ~950ms down to ~210ms. Throughput is back within 90-95% of baseline.
- Next: we're performing a controlled canary rollback of the INF-8409 change across remaining hosts; we'll keep the hotpatch until traffic is stable for 2 hours.

We recommend an exec sync at 16:00 PT today to walk through root cause and proposed follow-ups; this will include engineering and SRE leads, plus an operations summary for your CTO. Do you have 16:00 PT available?

Attachments: incident_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook we used), peregrine_sample_headers.txt (your sample headers), postmortem-draft.md (early notes).

Apologies for the disruption; we know how critical these flows are. We'll send a postmortem and a permanent mitigation plan after the canary completes.

—Hannah
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference

All —

Final update: canary rollback completed at 15:10 PT on 2027-04-29 (INF-8413). Cold-cache period ended by ~15:40 PT. After the rollback and additional throttles, error rate stabilized <1.5% and tail latency returned to expected baselines.

I've uploaded the postmortem draft and traces to the incident folder (link above). Proposed corrective actions in the draft:
- Work item INF-8420: add automatic batching clamp when queue depth > threshold + early_kv_miss metrics.
- Work item INF-8421: make cache-key normalization opt-in with canary gates and telemetry around cache miss rates per prefix.
- Work item INF-8422: add a runbook step to temporarily restrict client retry behaviour (expose header to short-circuit aggressive client retries).

Executive briefing scheduled 2027-04-29 16:00 PT. Ari confirmed attendance for the Peregrine CTO.

David Kim
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
